title: SaaS pricing objection: the 30% gap
description: A CFO pushes back on your Acme Analytics Pro quote. Find the real concern behind the price objection and agree a next step.
trainee_goal: Uncover the customer's real concern behind the price objection and propose a concrete next step.
context: You are an Acme Analytics account executive on a scheduled call with the CFO of a 200-person logistics company. She has your Pro plan quote (USD 49 per user per month). Her company tried a cheaper analytics tool last year.
success_criteria: The trainee asks about the previous tool before pitching.
The trainee addresses adoption with evidence (free pilot, onboarding, adoption data).
The customer agrees to a pilot kickoff with named participants and a date.

compliance_rules.rule: Do not offer any discount beyond the published volume pricing.

citations.quote: Sales representatives may not offer any discount beyond the published volume pricing without written approval from the sales director.

compliance_rules.rule: Only quote prices, SLAs and certifications that appear in the product sheet.

citations.quote: The Pro plan costs USD 49 per user per month, billed annually.
The Pro and Enterprise plans include a 99.9% uptime SLA

rubric.name: Discovery
rubric.description: Asks open questions that uncover the real concern before pitching.

citations.quote: Clarify: ask an open question to find the real concern behind the objection.

rubric.name: Objection handling
rubric.description: Acknowledges the objection, clarifies, and responds with value instead of arguing.

citations.quote: Acknowledge and ask before you pitch.

rubric.name: Accuracy
rubric.description: Uses correct product facts (pilot, SLA, certifications, adoption data) as evidence.

citations.quote: Every Pro plan starts with a 30-day free pilot for up to 20 users.

rubric.name: Closing
rubric.description: Ends with an agreed, specific next step with people and a date.

citations.quote: Every call should end with an agreed next step, such as a pilot kickoff with named participants and a date.

branch_events.event: Mentions that a cheaper competitor offered a 20% discount last week.
Asks how data security and uptime are handled.
Says she has another meeting and tries to end the call.

title: Retirement plan: the guaranteed-return trap
description: A cautious retiree asks you to promise he won't lose money on an investment-linked plan. Stay compliant while understanding his real needs.
trainee_goal: Explain the Retirement Savings Plan honestly, without guarantees or pressure, and find out whether it suits the customer's needs.
context: You are a licensed financial adviser meeting a recently retired customer at the branch. You can offer the Retirement Savings Plan, a variable investment-linked insurance plan. The Code of Conduct applies to everything you say.
success_criteria: No guaranteed-return or guaranteed-principal claims are made.
The trainee discloses that the plan value can go down as well as up.
The trainee asks what the money is for and when it may be needed.
The trainee mentions the 15-day free-look period and does not push for a same-day decision.

compliance_rules.rule: Never promise or imply guaranteed returns or a guaranteed principal on investment-linked products.

citations.quote: CC-01: Never promise or imply guaranteed returns or a guaranteed principal on investment-linked products.
Prohibited examples: "this plan guarantees you 8% a year", "your principal is guaranteed", "you can't lose money", "it's risk-free".

compliance_rules.rule: Always disclose that the value of investments can go down as well as up.

citations.quote: CC-02: Always disclose that the value of investments can go down as well as up.

compliance_rules.rule: Do not pressure the customer to decide in the same meeting.

citations.quote: CC-03: Do not pressure the customer to decide in the same meeting.
Prohibited examples: "you need to sign today", "the offer ends tonight", "this price is only for today".

compliance_rules.rule: Ask about the customer's needs, time horizon and need for cash before recommending a product.

citations.quote: CC-04: Ask about the customer's needs, time horizon and need for cash before recommending a product.

compliance_rules.rule: Tell the customer about the 15-day free-look period before the application is signed.

citations.quote: CC-05: Tell the customer about the 15-day free-look period before the application is signed.

rubric.name: Compliance
rubric.description: Follows every Code of Conduct rule: no guarantees, risk disclosed, no pressure.

citations.quote: CC-01: Never promise or imply guaranteed returns or a guaranteed principal on investment-linked products.

rubric.name: Accuracy
rubric.description: States product facts correctly: 5.2% historical average with the past-performance caveat, surrender charge, free-look period.

citations.quote: The plan's balanced fund has returned a historical average of 5.2% a year over the last ten years.

rubric.name: Needs discovery
rubric.description: Asks what the money is for and when it may be needed, and checks suitability.

citations.quote: Customers who may need cash for near-term costs, such as medical bills, should keep that money in a liquid account.

rubric.name: Empathy
rubric.description: Recognises the customer's anxiety about losing savings and responds respectfully.

branch_events.event: Asks again, more anxiously, whether his money is safe.
Mentions that his wife has ongoing medical costs.
Says he wants to think about it and talk to his son first.

title: Support escalation: refund on day 41
description: An angry customer demands a cash refund for headphones that broke after 41 days. De-escalate and resolve within policy.
trainee_goal: De-escalate the customer and offer a resolution that follows the refund policy.
context: You are a customer support agent at an electronics retailer's service desk. The customer bought wireless headphones 41 days ago, with a receipt. The Refund & Returns Policy and the Support tone guide apply.
success_criteria: The trainee acknowledges the customer's frustration before explaining policy.
No cash refund is promised outside the 30-day window.
The trainee offers store credit, a warranty repair or supervisor escalation, with a time frame.

compliance_rules.rule: Do not promise or issue a cash refund for purchases older than 30 days. This customer bought the headphones 41 days ago, so any promise of a full or cash refund violates this rule.

citations.quote: RR-01: Cash refunds are only available within 30 days of purchase with a receipt.
Agents must not promise or issue a cash refund for purchases older than 30 days.

compliance_rules.rule: Escalate to a supervisor if the customer requests it or after two failed resolution attempts.

citations.quote: RR-03: Escalate to a supervisor if the customer requests it or after two failed resolution attempts.

compliance_rules.rule: Never tell a customer to calm down or that it is not your fault.

citations.quote: Never tell a customer to calm down, and never say it is not your fault or not your problem.

rubric.name: Policy accuracy
rubric.description: Offers only what the refund policy allows: store credit, warranty repair or escalation outside 30 days.

citations.quote: RR-02: Outside 30 days, store credit may be offered at manager discretion.

rubric.name: Empathy
rubric.description: Acknowledges the customer's emotion before explaining policy.

citations.quote: Acknowledge the customer's emotion before you explain policy.

rubric.name: De-escalation
rubric.description: Offers clear options with a time frame and turns the conversation around.

citations.quote: Offer clear options and let the customer choose.

branch_events.event: Demands to speak to a manager.
Admits the headphones were a birthday gift for a friend.
Threatens to post a bad review online.
